MAJOR: AC-4 ("precheck fast tier passes with rejected baseline items present and fails closed for unknown statuses") has no corresponding control, coverage entry, or test: test_matrix is entirely unit pytest against one file, so the approved design cannot evidence this end-to-end AC.

AC-1's "one shared predicate" is asserted but no test or static check proves the three gates actually import `gate_status.should_skip` rather than keeping local copies; behavioral tests alone permit silent re-forking of the terminal set.
MINOR: Status literals remain inconsistent across artifacts: AC says `won-t-do`/`wont-do`, FR edge_cases say `won't_do`/`wont_do`, failure_matrix says `won-t_do`/`wont_do`; an exact-match predicate using the wrong literal would fail closed on a supposedly terminal item.
`controls` and `implementation_controls` are byte-identical duplicated blocks — guaranteed drift as edits land in one and not the other.

Entrypoint contradiction: coverage/entrypoint lists `scripts/dev/gate_status.py:should_skip` while `runtime_contract.entrypoint` lists `scripts/dev/design_pack.py:should_enforce`; the single source of truth is ambiguous.

Skips are not observable: gate output reports only a checked count with no skipped-count or skip-reason, so diagnosing why an item was skipped requires reading code (guardrail 10 minimum diagnostics).
Control kinds are mislabeled (C-2 `kind: config`, C-3 `kind: security` for pure status predicates), misrouting review/security scoping for a tooling-only change.
NIT: Test file `test_gates_skip_rejected.py` under-describes coverage of cancelled/won't-do/live/unknown statuses.
`functional_sha` (a38a9e99c9fb) still differs from all `candidate_sha` (bc5a6145) despite the prior disposition claiming this traceability item was ACTIONED.
SUMMARY: Sound approach overall: shared pure predicate, fail-closed unknown handling, tooling-only Python (language rule compliant), and no data/API/security surface.
Top risks: AC-4 lacks any precheck-level evidence in the approved controls/tests, and the shared-predicate invariant is asserted rather than structurally enforced.
Residual artifact-hygiene issues (literal mismatches, duplicated control blocks, contradictory entrypoints) undermine the traceability the design is meant to restore.
